title_tag: Housecall Pro Review (2026): Honest Pricing, Pros & Cons
title: Housecall Pro: More Tool Than Most Shops Need
meta: Honest Housecall Pro review for contractors in 2026: real pricing (Basic/Essentials/Max), the financing and proposal tools it does well, the Android-app and support complaints, and who should pick it over Jobber.
dek: Housecall Pro does more than Jobber — built-in consumer financing, instant payouts, slick proposals — and charges more for it. Whether that's worth it comes down to one question: do you have techs to dispatch and jobs big enough to finance, or are you a two-truck shop paying for features you'll never open?
verdict_text: Conditional yes. If you run multiple techs and want financing, instant payouts, and strong proposals in one place, Housecall Pro earns its price. If you're a small crew that mostly needs quote-schedule-invoice, Jobber does it for less. Watch the add-ons and the ~2.59% card processing — the headline plan isn't the real bill.

blocks.h: Where it beats the cheaper option
blocks.html: Housecall Pro is a full field-service platform — scheduling, dispatch, invoicing, CRM — with extras most competitors don't bundle: consumer financing you can offer at the door, instant payouts (Instapay), expense cards, and a stronger proposal / upsell toolkit. For a shop running several techs and selling bigger-ticket work, those tools move money. It's a real, well-built product with high ratings — 4.7/5 on Capterra across thousands of reviews.

blocks.label: Fair warning
blocks.claim: “Everything your business needs in one app.”
blocks.small: Mostly true — but the recurring complaints are real: the Android app lags the iOS one (a years-long gripe), support response can be slow, and the sales outreach is aggressive. And the all-in cost (seats + add-ons + ~2.59% processing) runs well above the sticker. Great tool; just don't buy the Max plan to use a third of it.

faq.q: Is Housecall Pro worth it in 2026?
faq.a: For shops running multiple techs that want built-in financing, instant payouts, and strong proposals, yes — it earns its higher price. For a solo operator or very small crew that mainly needs quoting, scheduling, and invoicing, Jobber usually delivers the same core for less.

faq.q: How much does Housecall Pro really cost?
faq.a: List plans run roughly $79 (Basic, 1 user), $189 (Essentials, up to 5), and $329 (Max, up to 8) month-to-month, lower annually. The real bill is higher once you add seats, add-ons, and card processing (~2.59%) — budget $150–$350/mo all-in for a typical small shop.

faq.q: What are the biggest Housecall Pro complaints?
faq.a: The most consistent ones are a weaker Android app than iOS, inconsistent support response times, and aggressive sales/upsell outreach. The core product is well-rated (4.7/5 on Capterra), but those three come up repeatedly.
